5.speaker: Lucian Galade
5.text: “Is the welcome to your liking, sir?”

6.speaker: Narrator
6.text: Dwight Walker, President of Arcasia, Head of the ATO came out of the car, smiling and waving at the enormous crowd that gathered. It was not every day an Arcasian president came to visit Sordland after all.

7.speaker: Narrator
7.text: Both sides of the maroon carpet leading up to the palace were lined up with soldiers wearing military uniforms of the Kingdom of Sordland era. They had swords, shields, spears and some of them were on horseback.

14.speaker: Narrator
14.text: As soon as President Walker stepped on the carpet, children appeared and showered the road with roses. He slowly started walking towards us.

15.speaker: Narrator
15.text: Lucian approached my side and quietly whispered.

16.speaker: Narrator
16.text: It was then the centuries old Sordish sword dance started. The show took a minute at most and President Walker watched it quietly with a stern face, nodding.

17.speaker: Player
17.text: “What I meant with extravagant was not a circus show. What the hell is this?”

19.speaker: Player
19.text: “As long as it does the trick, I don't care.”

20.speaker: Lucian Galade
20.text: “But... but I don't understand, sir. I did everything you asked.”

23.speaker: Narrator
23.text: Seeing that President Walker was approaching, Lucian stood back.

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Finally, I was in reaching distance to one of the most powerful men in the world.

25.speaker: Narrator
25.text: He looked at Monica first, bowed and kissed her hand for a second longer than I'd like.

26.speaker: Dwight Walker
26.text: “Mr. Rayne. If you told me I would get to meet with your lovely wife, I would've come sooner.”

27.speaker: Monica
27.text: “Oh my. Thank you, Mr. Walker. It's a pleasure to meet with you.”

29.speaker: Dwight Walker
29.text: “The pleasure is all mine, Ms. Rayne.”

30.speaker: Dwight Walker
30.text: “Mr. President. It is so good to finally meet with you.”

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “I wanted to meet with you for the longest time.”

34.speaker: Player
34.text: “It is really good to see you, Mr. President.”

35.speaker: Dwight Walker
35.text: “I assure you, the feeling is mutual. That's why I am here in fact.”

37.speaker: Narrator
37.text: We started walking towards the reception hall in the palace. Our path was cleared of people at once.

39.speaker: Monica
39.text: “I hope your wife and the family is well.”

40.speaker: Dwight Walker
40.text: “They are very well, Ms. Rayne. Thank you. Unfortunately they couldn't make it here today.”

42.speaker: Narrator
42.text: As soon as President Walker stepped on the carpet, all of the soldiers performed a hard salute. Celebratory gunshots were fired. Trumpets started playing a Sordish march.

43.speaker: Narrator
43.text: Along with Monica, I started walking over to meet him mid way.

44.speaker: Dwight Walker
44.text: “Mr. President. One would think you are prepared to go to war with me instead.”

88.speaker: Dwight Walker
88.text: “I was almost going to think that you weren't expecting me.”

89.speaker: Player
89.text: “We are very sorry to hear that.”

90.speaker: Player
90.text: “I'm a simple man. Not really a fan of extravagance.”

91.speaker: Player
91.text: “Of course not! You are our guest of honor!”

93.speaker: Dwight Walker
93.text: “Me, Mr. President... I am the exact opposite.”

106.speaker: Narrator
106.text: He was simply looking around at the extraordinary interior design of the Maroon Palace. Statues, paintings and various ornaments filled both sides of the corridor.

107.speaker: Narrator
107.text: We passed the corridor and entered the reception hall. The crowd inside was composed of various politicians and state figures.

108.speaker: Narrator
108.text: Upon our entry, they started clapping. Dry martinis were handed to both of us.

109.speaker: Player
109.text: “Don't mind us. We were just passing by.”

110.speaker: Player
110.text: “Ladies and gentlemen. I present to you, President Walker.”

111.speaker: Player
111.text: “Everyone. Let's give a warm welcome to our guest of honor.”

112.speaker: Dwight Walker
112.text: “Thank you. President Rayne. It is really good to be here.”

113.speaker: Dwight Walker
113.text: “And thank you everyone for the warm welcome.”

115.speaker: Narrator
115.text: With another thunderous round of applause, the jazz band started playing.

117.speaker: Narrator
117.text: President Walker and I separated and started mingling with the crowd. The reception was in full swing.

118.speaker: Narrator
118.text: She looked over at me before smiling at him.

119.speaker: Narrator
119.text: After some time chatting with the attendees, President Walker approached us. He bowed before my wife.

120.speaker: Dwight Walker
120.text: “Ms. Rayne. Can I call you Monica?”

121.speaker: Monica
121.text: “Yes, of course. If I can call you Dwight.”

122.speaker: Narrator
122.text: He took her hand and they started dancing. I turned around to talk to the waiter.

123.speaker: Narrator
123.text: I was into my third martini when I heard a whistle. I turned around and saw Monica, dancing very closely with President Walker. All eyes in the room were on them.

125.speaker: Player
125.text: “President Walker, why don't we have a chat somewhere quiet?”

126.speaker: Player_Italic
126.text: Interject and dance with Monica yourself.

128.speaker: Dwight Walker
128.text: “Right when we were getting to the good part."

130.speaker: Narrator
130.text: The band played on. For a moment, it felt like it was only the two of us in the room. We moved together as one, seamlessly gliding across the dance floor.

131.speaker: Narrator
131.text: We hadn't danced since our wedding. I was struggling to remember the right steps. President Walker was watching us with his arms crossed and a smile on his face.

133.speaker: Narrator
133.text: As Monica whispered the steps in my ear, I followed along -- at first hesitantly, then smoother and more confident. It was starting to come back to me.

134.speaker: Narrator
134.text: At some point, a spotlight began shining on us. As the song came to an end, I spun Monica around and dramatically dipped her on the last beat.

135.speaker: Narrator
135.text: Applause and whistles echoed around us. We went back to the bar.

136.speaker: Narrator
136.text: President Walker approached, clapping and whistling himself.

138.speaker: Dwight Walker
138.text: “I never took you for a dancer, Mr. Rayne.”

141.speaker: Player
141.text: “I thought I would mess it up.”

142.speaker: Dwight Walker
142.text: “I'm beginning to see how you landed such a beautiful wife."

143.speaker: Dwight Walker
143.text: “I do practice in my free time but, I could never hope to be as good as you.”

145.speaker: Dwight Walker
145.text: “Let's talk about some business, shall we?”

146.speaker: Narrator
146.text: The waiter came by and we swapped our empty glasses with filled ones.

147.speaker: Narrator
147.text: Swirling around, Monica looked like she was having fun.

148.speaker: Narrator
148.text: They finally finished their dance after a few minutes and came over to the bar that I was leaning on.

150.speaker: Dwight Walker
150.text: “And Mr. Rayne. You are one lucky guy.”

151.speaker: Player
151.text: “I know, and I cherish every moment of it.”

152.speaker: Player
152.text: “We had enough fun. Let's talk about business.”

153.speaker: Player
153.text: “I hope you enjoyed your little dance.”

155.speaker: Dwight Walker
155.text: “I think we both did, right Monica?”

156.speaker: Monica
156.text: “Yes, Dwight. Thank you for accompanying me.”

157.speaker: Narrator
157.text: Monica looked at me and smiled.

160.speaker: Dwight Walker
160.text: “Right when I was just getting started.”

161.speaker: Narrator
161.text: The President and I swapped our drinks for Erlory Maroon 30 year olds. I knew a special spot. With our drinks at hand, we went down the stairs to the basement.

162.speaker: Narrator
162.text: He took a seat and I followed suit. He pulled out two cigars.

165.speaker: Narrator
165.text: Gradually, the music and the sound of the party started to fade away.

166.speaker: Narrator
166.text: We arrived at a cozy little corner office with not much inside other than a table and comfortable chairs.

167.speaker: Dwight Walker
167.text: “These are the best cigars in the world. I guarantee it. Are you sure?”

169.speaker: Player
169.text: “Well, when you put it like that... sure.”

170.speaker: Narrator
170.text: He pulled out a Rippo lighter and lit my cigar before lighting his own.

171.speaker: Narrator
171.text: He pulled out a Rippo lighter and lit his cigar.

172.speaker: Narrator
172.text: We clinked our glasses and took a sip.

173.speaker: Dwight Walker
173.text: “Ah. This is a really good one. Very smoky. I like it.”

176.speaker: Player_Italic
176.text: Wait for him to start the conversation.

177.speaker: Narrator
177.text: He took a puff from his cigar, filling the small room with smoke.

179.speaker: Dwight Walker
179.text: “But, I like Lespian whiskey more. It pairs better with their cigars.”

180.speaker: Dwight Walker
180.text: “You see, Mr. Rayne. Whiskeys are a little bit like countries.”

181.speaker: Dwight Walker
181.text: “Some are stronger, some are weaker. Some are older, some are younger. Many are complex but sometimes simple is the best.”

182.speaker: Dwight Walker
182.text: “I personally like stronger whiskeys in general. That's why I liked this one. Yes. It is definitely promising.”

183.speaker: Dwight Walker
183.text: “But whatever you drink, in the end, it all boils down to your own taste. And I assure you, Mr. Rayne. My sense of taste is *very* refined.”

184.speaker: Dwight Walker
184.text: “What type of whiskey do you like?”

187.speaker: Player
187.text: “I am good with whatever is made here in Sordland.”

188.speaker: Dwight Walker
188.text: “A fine answer but a bit restricted, I would say.”

193.speaker: Dwight Walker
193.text: “As good as they are, they can get tiring.”

195.speaker: Narrator
195.text: He tugged at his tie to loosen it a little.

196.speaker: Dwight Walker
196.text: “I want to make you an offer.”

200.speaker: Dwight Walker
200.text: “Of course not. This is an offer. Not an order.”

206.speaker: Dwight Walker
206.text: “I heard you got into a scandal. Something about a secretary.”

207.speaker: Player
207.text: “Let's not talk about the scandal. We have much more important matters to discuss.”

211.speaker: Dwight Walker
211.text: “Relax. It's just a scandal and I'm no reporter.”

213.speaker: Dwight Walker
213.text: “I just made it out alive of a bad one myself. Oof. It was a rough one too.”

214.speaker: Dwight Walker
214.text: “You get used to it. A couple of people in prison, couple people silenced... you know the drill.”

215.speaker: Dwight Walker
215.text: “Cheers to your survival then, Mr. Rayne.”

220.speaker: Dwight Walker
220.text: “I know that you are preparing to go to war against Rumburg.”

224.speaker: Dwight Walker
224.text: “And that your embargo on United Contana makes me the only superpower that you can align with.”

225.speaker: Dwight Walker
225.text: “I am willing to support you in your endeavour.”

229.speaker: Dwight Walker
229.text: “But understand that I am saying this despite your attempts to get closer to Valgsland.”

233.speaker: Dwight Walker
233.text: “But understand that I am saying this despite your previous actions.”
233.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_FPnT_ATO_Against"] == true) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Valgsland_Alliance"] == true  or  Variable["BaseGame.Valgsland_HeljilandRecognised"] == true) == false)

234.speaker: Dwight Walker
234.text: “And that has a price. So here is my offer.”

238.speaker: Dwight Walker
238.text: “I think there is much we can achieve together and you have shown me the proof.”

239.speaker: Dwight Walker
239.text: “ATO will generously welcome you as a member state. You will have all privileges and responsibilities that come with it. I want to underline responsibilities.”

240.speaker: Dwight Walker
240.text: “In return, ATO will attach as a parallel military structure next to the Sordish military. That includes all branches. Air, navy, army. We will provide our very own Generals to work alongside the Sordish command.”

241.speaker: Dwight Walker
241.text: “Please try to understand me, Mr. Rayne. Under normal circumstances, this is not required of ATO members. But this is the price I am putting on the survival of your country.”

242.speaker: Dwight Walker
242.text: “If you ask me it is a generous price in return for all the privileges you will receive.”

243.speaker: Dwight Walker
243.text: “If you accept, I would like to extend you a warm welcome to ATO as a full member state. This of course comes along with lots of privileges and responsibilities.”
243.conditionsRaw: ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_FPnT_ATO_Against"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGameIsolated.Turn09_FPnT_ATO_Aligned"] == true) == false) and ((Variable["BaseGame.Lespia_Alliance"] == true) == false)

244.speaker: Dwight Walker
244.text: “Join us, Mr. Rayne and you will have the entire backing of ATO. Soldiers, jet fighters, warships... whatever you like.”

245.speaker: Dwight Walker
245.text: “All I ask in return is mutual loyalty to one another in the pact.”

249.speaker: Dwight Walker
249.text: “A friend of Lespia is our friend as well.”

250.speaker: Dwight Walker
250.text: “Let's make history. Here. Tonight. What do you say?”

251.speaker: Dwight Walker
251.text: “In ATO, we protect each other. We have a mutual defense clause in the case of war.”

252.speaker: Dwight Walker
252.text: “During peacetime, you will see the effects even more! Our combined production output will benefit both Sordland and ATO. We will have free-trade zone agreements, free visa access, investments, you name it.”

253.speaker: Dwight Walker
253.text: “Before you answer, let me assure you. If you reject my kind offer, you won't like the results.”

254.speaker: Player
254.text: “Do you dare threaten me here, in my palace?”

255.speaker: Dwight Walker
255.text: “Hah. Yes I am. It wouldn't be my first time threatening a president in his palace either.”

256.speaker: Player
256.text: “I accept, Mr. Walker. [Join ATO, Break Alliance with Valgsland, -2 Government Budget]”

257.speaker: Player
257.text: “You can't expect me to hand over the military command to you.”

258.speaker: Dwight Walker
258.text: “So, what will it be, Mr. Rayne? Will you be able to protect your own country at the cost of your own pride?”

259.speaker: Dwight Walker
259.text: “You won't be handing over the entire military command. Only a part of it.”

260.speaker: Dwight Walker
260.text: “Besides, that part is not up for negotiation. Take it or leave it. Your choice.”

262.speaker: Player
262.text: “It appears that I thought wrongly about you. I decline, Mr. Walker.”

263.speaker: Dwight Walker
263.text: “Then that's too bad. You have doomed your country, Mr. Rayne.”

264.speaker: Dwight Walker
264.text: “May God help you and your country.”

265.speaker: Player
265.text: “Very well. I accept. [Join ATO, Break Alliance with Valgsland, -2 Government Budget]”

267.speaker: Dwight Walker
267.text: “Welcome to ATO, Mr. Rayne. Welcome home.”

268.speaker: Narrator
268.text: We stood up and shook hands.

270.speaker: Narrator
270.text: We clinked our glasses and downed the remaining whiskey.

272.speaker: Dwight Walker
272.text: “Let's go upstairs, Mr. Rayne. We have much to discuss.”

273.speaker: Dwight Walker
273.text: “But, more importantly... we need to celebrate!”

274.speaker: Narrator
274.text: He grabbed his glass and downed the remaining whiskey.

276.speaker: Dwight Walker
276.text: “I'm going upstairs to join the party to wash the bad taste left in my mouth.”

278.speaker: Dwight Walker
278.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Agnolia_Alliance"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Valgsland_Alliance"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Lespia_Alliance"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Wehlen_JointOperation"] == false) == false

279.speaker: Player
279.text: “I say aye! I accept, Mr. Walker.  [Join ATO, Break Alliance with Valgsland, -2 Government Budget]”

280.speaker: Player
280.text: “Thank you for the offer however, we currently have no plans to enter ATO.”

281.speaker: Player
281.text: “I assure you we can hold our own against Rumburg just fine.”

282.speaker: Dwight Walker
282.text: “I didn't mean any offence, Mr. Rayne. I am fully aware of the capabilities of the mighty Sordish Armed Forces.”

283.speaker: Player
283.text: “Is that all you are asking for? I was expecting more demands.”

284.speaker: Dwight Walker
284.text: “But, why, Mr. Rayne? In my mind we are already aligned.”

285.speaker: Dwight Walker
285.text: “Where I am coming is more so from the perspective of friendship and stability in Eastern Merkopa.”

286.speaker: Dwight Walker
286.text: “There is much to gain for both of us which makes this the perfect partnership.”

287.speaker: Dwight Walker
287.text: “At least I know that I tried.”

288.speaker: Dwight Walker
288.text: “Don't close yourself to the opportunity. Maybe you are not ready now but you might be ready in the future.”

289.speaker: Dwight Walker
289.text: “I usually get what I want, Mr. Rayne and trust me, you won't get rid of me that easily.”

290.speaker: Narrator
290.text: He smiled and we shook hands.

291.speaker: Player
291.text: “Unfortunately I can't accept your offer, Mr. Walker.”

292.speaker: Player
292.text: “Very well. I accept. [Join ATO, Break Alliance with Valgsland, -2 Government Budget]”

293.speaker: Dwight Walker
293.text: “Regardless, it was good to meet with you. I hope this is the start of something good.”

294.speaker: Narrator
294.text: He grabbed his glass and downed the remaining whiskey.

296.speaker: Dwight Walker
296.text: “Let's go upstairs, Mr. Rayne and join the party, Mr. Rayne.”

297.speaker: Dwight Walker
297.text: “I have a few more dance moves to show off.”
297.conditionsRaw: (Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Agnolia_Alliance"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Valgsland_Alliance"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Lespia_Alliance"] == false  and  Variable["BaseGame.Policy_Diplomacy_Wehlen_JointOperation"] == false) == false

298.speaker: Dwight Walker
298.text: “Besides, I have a few more dance moves to show off.”

299.speaker: Dwight Walker
299.text: “Times are changing and so is the balance of the world.”

303.speaker: Dwight Walker
303.text: “Besides, your embargo on United Contana makes ATO the only side that you can align with.”

304.speaker: Dwight Walker
304.text: “Soon, instead of a fractured world, we will see a more united world. There is us, ATO against them.”

305.speaker: Dwight Walker
305.text: “I want you by our side. The winning side.”

309.speaker: Player
309.text: “I assure you we can hold out our own just fine.”

311.speaker: Narrator
311.text: Next to the maroon carpet to the palace, Sordish troops were lined up. Sordish war planes flew above our heads, painting the sky with the colors of the Sordish flag.

315.speaker: Narrator
315.text: On the way to the entrance we stopped in front of Iosef who was in charge of the troops.

316.speaker: Narrator
316.text: President Walker saluted him and the soldiers. They saluted back.

317.speaker: Narrator
317.text: As soon as our inspection finished, we entered the palace.

318.speaker: Dwight Walker
318.text: “The Sordish Armed Forces will be a member of the ATO military structure. All branches be it air, navy, army will collaborate with the alliance network. We will provide assistance and training for free.”

319.speaker: Dwight Walker
319.text: “Our armies will learn how to fight together and be stronger than ever in the face of the Malenyevist threat!”

320.speaker: Player
320.text: "I can't believe we pulled that off."

325.speaker: Monica
325.text: "Next time, let me take care of myself."

327.speaker: Narrator
327.text: Monica blinked and abruptly removed her hand from mine.

331.speaker: Narrator
331.text: Monica gave me an extremely strained smile.

335.speaker: Narrator
335.text: Behind his back, she grimaced at me and exaggeratedly held her nose.

336.speaker: Narrator
336.text: Behind his back, she gave me a taunting look.

340.speaker: Dwight Walker
340.text: “As you know, Arcasia is a country that has freedom at its very foundation. Anyone is welcome.”

341.speaker: Dwight Walker
341.text: “But, make no mistake. I have no compassion for deserters.”

342.speaker: Dwight Walker
342.text: “It has come to my ears that two businessmen from your country are now living in Arcasia.”

343.speaker: Dwight Walker
343.text: “Their names are Marcel Koronti and Walter Tusk.”

344.speaker: Dwight Walker
344.text: “I can send them back to you if you want.”

345.speaker: Player
345.text: “Thank you, but there is no need. I don't care about them at all.”

346.speaker: Player
346.text: “Please do. They can't be living the good life after disrespecting me the way they did.”

347.speaker: Player
347.text: “This can't be for free. What do you want in return?”
